Strait of Hormuz Status: October 5, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  218 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
5 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.71 -0.53 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Oman is directing tankers to keep AIS transponders active while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, per TradeWinds News; this has not been independently confirmed in this feed.

02 Iran's closure conditions remain in place, per Iranian state media; DW reports Middle East oil exports have recovered to pre-war levels despite ongoing attacks, with producers routing shipments around the strait.

03 The product tanker Lipsi was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 4, left drifting after being hit in the engine room; the attacker has not been identified.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the focal point of a contested operational picture: Iranian state media maintain the strait is closed until Tehran's conditions are met, while DW, citing Kpler data, reports Middle East crude exports have recovered to pre-war levels despite continued attacks, with roughly 40 percent of Gulf crude leaving by routes that bypass the strait. TradeWinds News reports Oman has directed tankers to maintain AIS transponder activity while transiting the strait; that report has not been independently confirmed in this feed. The product tanker Lipsi was struck by a projectile on October 4, left drifting after the hit to her engine room; no party has been formally identified as responsible. LNG flows through the strait have extended a rebound begun in September, per gCaptain, as regional producers work to restore supplies. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; weekly publication means a multi-day lag is normal. Brent crude stood at $101.71, down 0.53 percent, as of 14:47 UTC. Forty-five events were indexed in the last 24 hours. As of 14:50 UTC, 202 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
